all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 introduced significant reforms to enhance the accuracy of corporate financial statements and established a new oversight body for accountants, aiming to restore investor confidence in financial reporting.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: By improving the reliability of financial reporting, the reform aims to enhance investor confidence, which can lead to increased investment and economic growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act was signed into law in 2002.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act represents a major overhaul of corporate governance and financial reporting standards, addressing systemic issues revealed by high-profile corporate scandals.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 created a new oversight body to supervise accountants, tightened the responsibility of corporate officers for financial reports and stiffened penalties.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on corporate financial reporting and oversight, which does not relate to R&D funding or innovation instruments.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Department of Health and Human Services has established a Patient Safety Task Force to identify and implement improvement strategies in healthcare quality.

all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The task force has been established and is operational.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The establishment of a task force represents a significant but narrower reform aimed at improving healthcare quality.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Department of Health and Human Services has established a Patient Safety Task Force to identify and implement improvement strategies.
